subject: science
edition: EPD Science Grade 6 textbook (English medium, 1st print 2014, 6th print 2019; 2015 NIE syllabus) + NIE Science Grade 6 Teachers' Guide, 1st ed. 2015

concepts.unit: 1. Wonders of the Living World (1.1 Characteristics of Organisms)
outcomes: Tell living things from non-living things and give examples of each
Describe the life characteristics: growth, reproduction, movement, respiration, nutrition and response
Plan a simple activity that shows a characteristic of life, such as plant growth
Record observations of organisms in a table and display the data
concepts.guideRef: Competency 1, level 1.1; TG pp. 2-3; syllabus p. xiii

concepts.title_en: Classifying Organisms: Plants, Animals and Microorganisms
concepts.unit: 1. Wonders of the Living World (1.2 Differences between Plants and Animals)
outcomes: Group organisms as plants, animals or microorganisms
Explain how plants and animals differ in locomotion, nutrition and growth
Use a simple dichotomous key to identify organisms
Show care for living things and value the diversity of life
concepts.guideRef: Competency 1, level 1.2; TG pp. 2-3; syllabus p. xiii

concepts.title_en: Things Around Us: Matter, Energy and States of Matter
outcomes: Distinguish matter from energy with everyday examples
Compare solids, liquids and gases by their shape and volume
Test solids for hardness, malleability, ductility, elasticity, brittleness and texture
Link material properties to how the materials are used
concepts.guideRef: Competency 2, levels 2.1-2.3; TG pp. 4-5; syllabus p. xiv

outcomes: Name the three states of water
Describe ground water, rain and surface water as water sources
Classify water as fresh, brackish or sea water, and compare salt content by experiment
Explain why water is vital and why it is a limited resource to conserve
concepts.guideRef: Competency 2, levels 2.4-2.6; TG pp. 6-7; syllabus p. xv

concepts.unit: 4. Energy in Day to Day Life
outcomes: Describe energy as the ability to do work
Identify the Sun as the main source of energy
Describe uses of biomass, fossil fuel, wind, hydro, wave, tidal, geothermal and nuclear energy
Recognise that some sources run out, and value using energy sustainably
concepts.guideRef: Competency 3, levels 3.1-3.3; TG p. 8; syllabus p. xvi

outcomes: State what is needed for us to see an object
Classify objects as luminous or non-luminous, and materials as transparent, translucent or opaque
Distinguish a light ray from a light beam, and show that light travels in straight lines
Describe everyday, medical and plant-growth uses of light
concepts.guideRef: Competency 3, levels 3.4-3.7; TG pp. 9-10; syllabus p. xvii

outcomes: Identify sound as what we sense with our ears
Classify sounds in the environment as natural or artificial
Tell music from noise
Make a simple instrument that produces sound by vibration
concepts.guideRef: Competency 3, levels 3.8-3.9; TG pp. 11-12; syllabus p. xviii

outcomes: Show that magnets attract certain materials only
Identify the poles of a magnet, including by using a compass
State that like poles repel and unlike poles attract
Use repulsion to tell a magnet from a piece of magnetic material
concepts.guideRef: Competency 3, levels 3.10-3.11; TG pp. 13-14; syllabus p. xviii

concepts.title_en: Electricity in Daily Life and How It Is Generated
outcomes: List everyday uses of electricity
Name devices and power stations that generate electricity
Describe chemical cells and solar cells as sources of electricity
Carry out a simple activity that generates electricity
concepts.guideRef: Competency 3, level 3.12; TG pp. 15-16; syllabus p. xix

concepts.title_en: Electric Circuits, Conductors and Electronic Components
outcomes: Connect a simple circuit with a cell, switch, bulb, wires and an ammeter
Draw circuit diagrams using standard symbols
Sort materials into conductors and insulators by testing them
Describe what diodes, LEDs, resistors and LDRs do, and use electricity safely and economically
concepts.guideRef: Competency 3, levels 3.13-3.14; TG pp. 15-16; syllabus p. xix

outcomes: List ways heat is generated: fuel, electricity, sunlight and friction
Measure temperature correctly with a thermometer
Demonstrate the effects of heat: temperature rise, expansion, change of state and change of colour
Relate the effects of heat to the environment, and handle heat safely
concepts.guideRef: Competency 3, levels 3.15-3.17; TG pp. 16-17; syllabus p. xx

outcomes: Classify animals as herbivores, carnivores or omnivores by what they eat
Explain that all animals depend directly or indirectly on plants for food
Build food chains from observations, and link them into food webs
Pick out food chains within a food web, and value the balance of nature
concepts.guideRef: Competency 4, levels 4.1-4.2; TG p. 18; syllabus p. xxi

outcomes: Distinguish weather from climate
Name rain, wind, temperature and humidity as factors that determine weather
Use simple home-made or standard instruments to observe and record weather over time
Describe floods, cyclones, droughts and landslides linked to climatic changes
concepts.guideRef: Competency 4, levels 4.3-4.4; TG pp. 19-20; syllabus p. xxii
